newsitem.title: USA: Israel finance minister calls for calm.
newsitem.headline: Israel finance minister calls for calm.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor called on Thursday for calm and a return to the negotiating table after the latest clashes between Israelis and Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Meridor, speaking to investors at the New York Stock Exchange, said he hoped Palestinians would act in a "sensibly and responsible" way after violence that has claimed 55 lives in the past two days.
"I hope people will be sensible and responsible to do whatever they can to calm things down," Meridor said. "We have to find a way to calm things down to go back to the negotiating process."

He expressed concern that Palestinian authorities would not have sufficient control over the protesters to quiet the demonstrations. By Thursday, 44 Palestinians and 11 Israelis had been reported killed in the unrest.
Palestinian protests erupted on Wednesday after Israel opened an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem, and clashes soon spread through the West Bank and Gaza.
"This was an excuse for an outburst of violence," Meridor said, referring to the opening of the tunnel. "We were in the process of solving the problem."
